text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Vietnam's year-on-year gross domestic product growth in the first six months of 1997 slipped to 9.1 percent from 9.2 percent in the first half of last year and 9.4 percent in the same period of 1995, the General Statistics Office reported. The decline was due to ineffective production and slow sales caused by a lack of capital, obsolete technology and poor management.
-- Overdue loans in Vietnamese dong will be subject to interest rates equivalent to 150 percent of lending rate ceilings.
-- The cabinet met on Monday and Tuesday to review the socio-economic performance of the first six months of this year and propose measures for improvements in the second half.
-- Death and life imprisonment sentences were upheld on Tuesday after the Supreme Court rejected appeals for leniency by defendants in Vietnam's biggest drug-trafficking case.

-- Output by industry with foreign investment, up 23 percent in the first half of this year from the same period in 1996, accounted for 25.4 percent of the country's total industrial production. Its revenue during the period was up 34 percent at $1.09 billion.
-- Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer is due to arrive in Hanoi on Wednesday for a five-day official visit.
